# Anchor-Align: Generalizable VLA Finetuning via Representation Anchoring and Language-Action Alignment

> Anchor-Align is a finetuning method for vision-language-action (VLA) models that prevents behavior cloning from overwriting the pretrained vision-language representations that support visual and semantic generalization. It adds two objectives to standard BC: Vision-Language Anchoring (layer-wise distillation from a frozen VLM copy) and Language-Action Alignment (joint language and action prediction on the same robot observation). Real-robot success improves from 28% to 54% and 37% to 60% across two VLA architectures on a physical xArm7, with consistent gains on LIBERO-PRO, LIBERO-Plus, and CALVIN.

Paper: arXiv:2607.13429 (cs.RO, cs.CV), 15 July 2026.
Authors: Dwip Dalal, Shivansh Patel, Chahit Jain, Jeonghwan Kim, Utkarsh Mishra, Alex Baratian, Hyeonjeong Ha, Heng Ji, Svetlana Lazebnik, Unnat Jain (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; Texas A&M University; University of California, Irvine).

## Problem addressed

- Behavior cloning finetuning of a pretrained VLM progressively overwrites pretrained representations, degrading out-of-distribution and semantic generalization in VLA policies.
- Co-training on web image-text data does not fix this, because language and action losses are applied to separate observations, which leaves language-action misalignment.
- Standard manipulation benchmarks do not expose this misalignment.

## Method

- Vision-Language Anchoring: distills layer-wise hidden representations from a frozen copy of the pretrained VLM into the policy during finetuning, preventing representation drift.
- Language-Action Alignment: converts each continuous action target into a discrete motion-direction label and trains language and action prediction jointly on the same robot observation.
